subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 30-year-old man finishes a marathon with a venous lactate of 11 mmol/L. Over the next few hours his blood lactate falls to 1.5 mmol/L while his plasma glucose is maintained at 88 mg/dL, and his liver takes up lactate and releases glucose. His resting oxygen consumption increases modestly during recovery.
question: How many high-energy phosphate bonds are consumed in the liver to convert the lactate produced by anaerobic glycolysis of 1 mol of blood glucose back into 1 mol of glucose?
explanation_correct: Gluconeogenesis from 2 mol of pyruvate consumes 4 ATP (2 in the pyruvate carboxylase reaction and 2 in the phosphoglycerate kinase reaction) plus 2 GTP in the phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase reaction, for a total of 6 high-energy phosphate bonds per glucose formed. Because anaerobic glycolysis of 1 mol of glucose yields only 2 mol of ATP, the Cori cycle shifts the energetic cost of recycling lactate to the liver.

explanation_incorrect.A: Two is the net ATP yield of anaerobic glycolysis per glucose, not the cost of gluconeogenesis.
explanation_incorrect.C: Four ATP are consumed by pyruvate carboxylase and phosphoglycerate kinase, but the 2 GTP used by phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase are additional.
explanation_incorrect.D: Eight overestimates the cost; no gluconeogenic step consumes additional high-energy phosphates beyond the 4 ATP and 2 GTP.
explanation_incorrect.E: Twelve would double the actual cost of 6 high-energy bonds per glucose formed.

educationalObjective: Converting 2 lactate molecules back to 1 glucose consumes 6 high-energy phosphate bonds (4 ATP and 2 GTP), making the Cori cycle energetically expensive.
